title: Base Color and the lit result
body: Default Lit uses the tinted texture as Base Color.
Change Roughness while keeping lighting and exposure fixed.
notes: This material uses the same sample and tint, but sends the result to Base Color in a Default Lit material. Roughness is a separate scalar input. title: Color building blocks

functions.name: Multiply / Add
functions.use: Tint a sampled color; scale or offset a value.
functions.glsl:
vec3 color = tex.rgb * tint;
float y = x * scale + bias;
functions.hlsl:
float3 color = tex.rgb * Tint;
float y = x * Scale + Bias;
functions.nodes:
Multiply: A × B
Add: A + B
functions.check: Multiplication is component-wise. A scalar scales every component. Multiplying by white preserves RGB; by black removes it.
functions.tryit: Set tint to (1, 0.5, 0.5). Which channels remain unchanged?

functions.name: Mix / Lerp
functions.use: Use a mask to blend between two colors.
functions.check: Alpha 0 returns A; 1 returns B. Values outside 0..1 extrapolate. A color Alpha blends channels independently.
functions.tryit: Set Alpha to 0, .5 and 1 before connecting a texture.

functions.name: Clamp / Saturate
functions.use: Keep a response within an intended range.
functions.nodes:
Saturate: clamp to 0..1
Clamp: explicit Min / Max
functions.check: Clamping is not normalization or remapping: values outside the range collapse to the endpoints.

title: Masks and repeating values

functions.name: Step
functions.use: Build a sharp binary mask or lighting threshold.
functions.check: Result is 0 when x < edge and 1 otherwise. UE Step uses X for the value and Y for the edge; the code arguments put the edge first.
functions.tryit: Raise the edge and watch the bright region shrink.

functions.name: Smoothstep
functions.use: Turn a hard edge into a smooth transition.
functions.check: Keep Min < Max. This softens a value transition; it does not blur a texture or guarantee anti-aliasing.
functions.tryit: Increase Max − Min while keeping their midpoint fixed.

functions.name: Fract / Frac
functions.use: Repeat a ramp or make repeating procedural UV patterns.
functions.check: Result is x − floor(x), also for negative x. Explicit Frac creates derivative discontinuities; texture wrapping usually handles repeating UVs better.
functions.tryit: Compare fract(-.2) with fract(.8). Both are .8.

title: Coordinates and texture data

functions.name: Time + UV offset
functions.use: Scroll texture coordinates without moving geometry.
functions.glsl: vec2 uv2 = uv * tiles + seconds * speed;
functions.hlsl: float2 uv2 = UV * Tiles + Seconds * Speed;
functions.nodes:
TextureCoordinate × Tiles
→ Add(Time × speed), or Panner
functions.check: UV speed is repeats per second. Use a float2/vector with two meaningful channels. Mesh positions do not change.
functions.tryit: Reverse only speed.x. Predict the motion direction.

functions.name: Remap a signed field
functions.use: Convert a stored 0..1 channel into a signed UV offset.
functions.check: A sampled .5 becomes zero offset. Import data textures with sRGB OFF.
functions.tryit: Connect signed flow to UVs with a small strength such as .02.

functions.name: Components / Append
functions.use: Extract channels or assemble a vector.
functions.glsl:
vec2 flow = data.gb;
vec3 n = vec3(slope, 1.0);
functions.hlsl:
float2 flow = Data.gb;
float3 n = float3(Slope, 1.0);
functions.check: RGBA and XYZW name the same component positions. Appending does not normalize a direction.
functions.tryit: Preview only the green channel; then append two scalar controls.

title: Lighting building blocks

functions.name: Normalize + Dot
functions.use: Measure alignment between directions for diffuse light or masks.
functions.nodes:
Normalize N + Normalize L
→ DotProduct → Saturate
functions.check: Use nonzero vectors in the same space. L points toward the light. Dot of unit vectors ranges from -1 to 1 before clamping.
functions.tryit: Rotate L while holding N fixed. When does the response become zero?

functions.name: Power + view rim
functions.use: Make a controllable highlight near grazing view angles.
functions.check: Normalize N and V first. Higher positive power narrows the rim. This artistic mask alone is not a complete Fresnel reflectance model. UE Fresnel adds its own BaseReflectFractionIn parameter and expects a world-space normal.
functions.tryit: Compare Power 1, 3 and 6 using the same camera.

functions.name: Floor + bands
functions.use: Reduce a smooth light value to a chosen number of levels.
functions.check: x is clamped 0..1 and n is an integer ≥2. The Min keeps x=1 at the final level rather than making an extra band.
functions.tryit: Compare 2, 4 and 6 levels; keep the light still.

title: Motion and shader stages

functions.name: Sine / Cosine
functions.use: Create periodic motion for pulses or waves.
functions.nodes:
Sine: set Period to 6.283185
for a radian input
functions.check: Code sin/cos use radians. UE Sine/Cosine default Period is 1: an input of 1 completes a cycle. Alternatively divide radians by 2π and keep Period 1.
functions.tryit: For 1 cycle per second, use sin(seconds × 2π) in code, or Time → Sine with Period 1 in UE.

functions.name: Vertex displacement
functions.use: Change the visible surface shape, such as wave height.
functions.nodes:
World Position Offset
expects a world-space offset
functions.check: The GLSL example assumes a local +Z plane. UE WPO uses world units (normally cm), needs enough vertices, and does not automatically update collision. Vertex displacement also needs matching shading normals.
functions.tryit: Set height to 0, then 6 cm. Inspect the silhouette, not just highlights.

functions.name: DDX / DDY / Fwidth
functions.use: Estimate how a pixel-stage value changes across nearby fragments.
functions.glsl:
float width = fwidth(x);
vec3 nx = dFdx(N);
functions.hlsl:
float width = fwidth(X);
float3 nx = ddx(N);
functions.nodes:
DDX / DDY
Abs(DDX) + Abs(DDY) for fwidth
functions.check: These are screen derivatives, not an analytic object-space slope. Use in the pixel stage. Discontinuous control flow or values can make them unreliable.
functions.tryit: Optional: use fwidth to scale a procedural edge transition as the camera moves.
